Messages.Author: Chris Berger
Messages.Body:
The ruling on Form of Mist says that it can only be played if you need
stealth (or at least it did... I'm assuming it still does). By
extension, it is possible to need stealth when you are in combat, no?
If yes, then can I play Swiftness of the Stag at <SPI> about 10 times
during combat, and then FoM and continue my action at +10 stealth? If
not, why not? I'm under the impression that a dual-type card can be
played as either type (i.e. I can play it as a combat card if I am
blocking, so it doesn't need to be legal *both* as an action card and
an action modifier), so can I play the <SPI> level as a combat card?

On a similar note, can I play the <for><obf> level of Elemental
Stoicism as an action (which doesn't do anything, natch)? Why not?

I guess my point is that most of the split-discipline dual-type cards
don't say *when* they can be used. For some of them, it's obvious.
You can only gain intercept if you need it, and I *believe* it was
finally established in the Great 2nd Tradition Debate that you can
only need intercept if you're attempting to block. But some of the
cards seem to allow you to do silly things that aren't specifically
prohibited by the rules. I don't like the idea of using "common
sense" to determine when the card is playable, since common sense has
been shown to be not all that "common". Plus, what one person may do
accidentally, another may do to exploit the lack of a rule, and this
seems like it could lead to huge rules headaches at tournaments.

So what's the deal?

Messages.Author: Halcyan 2
Messages.Body:
>The ruling on Form of Mist says that it can only be played if you need
>stealth (or at least it did... I'm assuming it still does). By
>extension, it is possible to need stealth when you are in combat, no?

A lot of the time if you are in combat, then you need the stealth. You do *not*
need the stealth if the combat is the result of the action (Bum's Rush,
Ambush), or the result of something other than a block (Hidden Lurker, Fast
Reaction, Siren's Lure). Also, even if you are in a combat that is a result of
a block, corner-case scenarios might result in not needing the stealth (a
Weather Control kills your opponent's Raven Spy, etc.).

>If yes, then can I play Swiftness of the Stag at <SPI> about 10 times
>during combat, and then FoM and continue my action at +10 stealth? If
>not, why not? I'm under the impression that a dual-type card can be
>played as either type (i.e. I can play it as a combat card if I am
>blocking, so it doesn't need to be legal *both* as an action card and
>an action modifier), so can I play the <SPI> level as a combat card?

Although it should really be cleared up, I think in most cases, it's implicit
what type of card most versions are. It's a bit weird since Madrigal can be
played as an action modifier or reaction, but superior Swiftness of the Stag is
clearly an action modifier (not combat) card. Otherwise you'd have people
trying to play manuevers or presses outside of combat.

>On a similar note, can I play the <for><obf> level of Elemental
>Stoicism as an action (which doesn't do anything, natch)? Why not?

I don't think so. The superior is explicit in that it is an action. The other
versions don't have any such text. Anyway, the "remainder of combat" thing
would make a potential action fruitless or confusing at best.

Halcyan 2

In message <5287ede4.01122...@posting.google.com>,

>The ruling on Form of Mist says that it can only be played if you need
>stealth (or at least it did... I'm assuming it still does). By
>extension, it is possible to need stealth when you are in combat, no?

Not quite. You only "need" stealth at ANY time if there is a blocking
minion whose intercept equals or exceeds the stealth of the acting
minion.

Combat resulting from a successful block satisfies these conditions, so
you can play Form of Mist. Stanislava in combat after being blocked
hunting by a minion with a Raven Spy could NOT play Form of Mist, as the
Raven Spy's intercept is negated by her special. Weird and corner-case,
yes.

>If yes, then can I play Swiftness of the Stag at <SPI> about 10 times
>during combat, and then FoM and continue my action at +10 stealth? If

Nope. After you play the first Swiftness, there is no longer a blocking
minion whose intercept equals or exceeds the stealth of the acting
minion. You no longer need stealth -- you can play no additional StS,
and you can no longer play FoM as an action modifier.

(see below -- this may not even be legal in the first place).

>not, why not? I'm under the impression that a dual-type card can be
>played as either type (i.e. I can play it as a combat card if I am
>blocking, so it doesn't need to be legal *both* as an action card and
>an action modifier), so can I play the <SPI> level as a combat card?

A dual-type card can only be played in an appropriate situation -- you
couldn't play Aura Absorption to gain +1 intercept as an acting minion,
for example, even though it is an action modifier/reaction. While there
are plenty of precedents for playing action modifiers in combat, those
are all specifically effects which provide a combat-related effect AND
an action-modifier effect.

I don't believe you could even play the SPI level as a card.

>On a similar note, can I play the <for><obf> level of Elemental
>Stoicism as an action (which doesn't do anything, natch)? Why not?

That level is only playable as a combat card, because there must be a
"remainder of combat".

>I guess my point is that most of the split-discipline dual-type cards

Actually, I think they're ALL pretty obvious, myself. But.

>>as an action modifier, resulting in a truly ridiculous (and quite
>>illegal) situation.
>

Clarification: You can't play combat effects outside of combat, which
is why you can't just play Form of Mist superior to gain the stealth,
and bypass combat entirely.

You can only play combat effects while you are in combat.

>indicates that having a card that is played in combat and provides
>stealth at least isn't a ludicrous proposition.

Right. Form of Mist, Mirror Image, Shadow Body, etc., both provide a
combat effect (strike: combat ends), and an action-modifier effect
(continue the action as if unblocked). Form of Mist also adds +1
stealth. Since all of these provide a combat effect, all are legal to
play during combat, although they also modify the action.

Swiftness of the Stag's superior reads only "+1 stealth", which does not
provide a combat effect, only an action-modifier effect -- and therefore
is not legal to play during combat.

Messages.Author: Chris Berger
Messages.Body:
LSJ <vte...@white-wolf.com> wrote in message news:<3C2E78B1...@white-wolf.com>...

> The card states it is an action modifier or a combat card. It also list
> several effects.
>
> Two of the effects are so obviously combat effects and not action modifier
> effects so as not to need additional verbage to belabor the point.
>
> The other effect is so obviously an action modifier and not a combat
> effect so as not to require additional verbage to belabor the point.

If each effect were only allowed to be one type, then I'd have no
problem here (then you'd say Maneuver is a combat effect and Stealth
is the action modifier effect). However, many cards that are playable
as two different types have a single effect that can be played as
either type (Madrigal at mel/MEL can be either action modifier or
reaction, so why can't Swallowed By the Night at obf be either an
action modifier or a combat card?).

I know that at one time, a dual-type card could only be played if it
were legal as both types. That made poor Ritual of the Bitter Rose
even tougher to use than it already is, since you had to be both the
acting minion and in combat, i.e. using Amaranth in a Rush deck.

At some point, it was apparently decided that you could use a card as
either type. I had thought there was an explicit ruling to the effect
of "cards with more than one type can be played as either type", but I
couldn't find that in the online rulings. AFAICT, there is no mention
of multi-typed cards in the rulebook either. Older cards used to say
at the top "this card can be played as either an action modifier or a
combat card", but I would guess this has been replaced with
rules-text... somewhere.

Also, AFAIK, there isn't any ruling against using cards in ways that
"seem" wrong, or one that says you have to play a card in the way that
"seems" obvious.

I will probably never play a stealth card in combat (although it might
be a good way to cycle cards), but I don't like little logical
loopholes that need to be covered up with "oh, but common sense says
that that's an action modifier effect and that's a combat effect." I
suppose a ruling saying something to that effect would be better than
it just being implied, but in hindsight, it might've been nice to
explicitly type effects on multi-type cards.
